script: Twenty two thousand officers wrote letters home in early 1940, and every single one of them was already dead. Polish families received postcards from their fathers, husbands, and sons, all mailed from Soviet prison camps, all reassuring, all completely normal. What the families didn't know was that Soviet secret police had already executed nearly all of them, shot one by one in a forest and buried in mass graves. For the next fifty years, those same families were told their men were still missing, or had fled, or simply vanished without explanation. Some spent decades searching, writing letters to a government that had murdered their relatives and then lied to their faces about it. It wasn't until 1990 that the truth was officially admitted, long after most of those families had already died still waiting for an answer. Twenty two thousand officers wrote letters home in 1940, and their families waited fifty years for a truth that came too late.

title: Their Families Waited 50 Years for an Answer That Came Too Late
description:
In 1940, the USSR executed nearly 22,000 Polish officers, then let their families believe they were still alive for decades. The truth wasn't admitted until 1990.
